name: Uriah Forrest
bio: A Delegate and a Representative from Maryland; born near Leonardtown, St. Mary's County, Md., in 1756; received a limited schooling; served in the Revolutionary War, as a first lieutenant, captain, and major in Maryland forces, Flying Camp; wounded at the Battle of Germantown and lost a leg at the Battle of Brandywine; Delegate to the Confederation Congress in 1787; unsuccessful candidate for election to United States Senate for the First Congress in 1788; elected as a Pro-Administration candidate to the Third Congress and served until his resignation on November 8, 1794 (March 4, 1793-November 8, 1794); commissioned major general of Maryland Militia in 1795; clerk of the circuit court of the District of Columbia, 1800-1805; died on July 6, 1805, at his home, ``Rosedale,'' near Georgetown, D.C.; interment in Oak Hill Cemetery, Washington, D.C.
